title: Per-partition Prometheus gauges must drop revoked partitions' series, or alerts see stale values
answers: false IngestionAnalyticsSinglePartitionDelayed page for a partition that is not behind
pod keeps exporting metrics for partitions it no longer owns
how to clear gauge labels on partition revoke
body:
Symptom: on-call gets an IngestionAnalyticsSinglePartitionDelayed page for a partition that is not behind, often an idle partition, after a rebalance.
Root cause: nodejs/src/ingestion/ingestion-consumer.ts:latestOffsetTimestampGauge kept the series of partitions the pod gave up in a rebalance. That frozen value kept getting older, and the alert's `max by (groupId, topic, partition)` picked it up whenever the new owner had no series yet.
Fix pattern: pass a revoke hook as the second argument of kafkaConsumer.connect. In IngestionConsumer.onPartitionsRevoked, call `gauge.remove({ topic, partition, groupId: this.groupId })` for each revoked partition, using the full label set. After this, only the current owner exports a partition.
Constraints: this applies to any gauge labelled by partition that an alert aggregates with max or min. common_ingestion_latest_processed_timestamp_ms in the common ingestion consumer still has the same stale-series problem; it was left out of scope because the analytics alert does not read it. Trade-off: if a new owner stalls before it processes its first message, the partition has no series and this alert stays silent. The all-partitions and stopped-consuming alerts still catch a stalled lane.
Test: ingestion-consumer.serial.test.ts gets the hook with `jest.mocked(ingester['kafkaConsumer'].connect).mock.calls[0][1]`, then checks `latestOffsetTimestampGauge.get()` values filtered by groupId. Call `.reset()` on the gauge first, because the registry is global.
applies: nodejs ingestion consumers that export per-partition Prometheus metrics
